sample_unit: emergency department faculty physicians who completed both phases

links.outcome: Clinician-perceived burden, usability, note quality, satisfaction and preference between two scribes in side-by-side local pilot
links.effect: DAX favored on unadjusted burden (median 1.5 vs 2, p=0.025), PDQI-9 (39 vs 36.5, p=0.011) and satisfaction (9 vs 7.5, p=0.015); usability equal (SUS 73.5 vs 73.5); adjusted models showed order effects, no overall preference.
links.quote: DAX received higher satisfaction ratings (median likelihood-to-recommend: 9 vs. 7.5; p = 0.015), but adjusted models suggested these differences reflected order effects more than inherent tool differences.

screen.reason: Prospective crossover evaluation of two ambient AI scribe tools (DAX vs. Abridge) used by emergency physicians during live clinical shifts.
